    13  /-! # Laurent polynomials
    14  
    15  We introduce Laurent polynomials over a semiring `R`.  Mathematically, they are expressions of the
    16  form
    17  $$
    18  \sum_{i \in \mathbb{Z}} a_i T ^ i
    19  $$
    20  where the sum extends over a finite subset of `ℤ`.  Thus, negative exponents are allowed.  The
    21  coefficients come from the semiring `R` and the variable `T` commutes with everything.
    22  
    23  Since we are going to convert back and forth between polynomials and Laurent polynomials, we
    24  decided to maintain some distinction by using the symbol `T`, rather than `X`, as the variable for
    25  Laurent polynomials.
    26  
    27  ## Notation
    28  The symbol `R[T;T⁻¹]` stands for `LaurentPolynomial R`.  We also define
    29  
    30  * `C : R →+* R[T;T⁻¹]` the inclusion of constant polynomials, analogous to the one for `R[X]`;
    31  * `T : ℤ → R[T;T⁻¹]` the sequence of powers of the variable `T`.
    32  
    33  ## Implementation notes
    34  
    35  We define Laurent polynomials as `AddMonoidAlgebra R ℤ`.
    36  Thus, they are essentially `Finsupp`s `ℤ →₀ R`.
    37  This choice differs from the current irreducible design of `Polynomial`, that instead shields away
    38  the implementation via `Finsupp`s.  It is closer to the original definition of polynomials.
    39  
    40  As a consequence, `LaurentPolynomial` plays well with polynomials, but there is a little roughness
    41  in establishing the API, since the `Finsupp` implementation of `R[X]` is well-shielded.
    42  
    43  Unlike the case of polynomials, I felt that the exponent notation was not too easy to use, as only
    44  natural exponents would be allowed.  Moreover, in the end, it seems likely that we should aim to
    45  perform computations on exponents in `ℤ` anyway and separating this via the symbol `T` seems
    46  convenient.
    47  
    48  I made a *heavy* use of `simp` lemmas, aiming to bring Laurent polynomials to the form `C a * T n`.
    49  Any comments or suggestions for improvements is greatly appreciated!
    50  
"}]

    36  Thus, they are essentially `Finsupp`s `ℤ →₀ R`.
    37  This choice differs from the current irreducible design of `Polynomial`, that instead shields away
    38  the implementation via `Finsupp`s.  It is closer to the original definition of polynomials.

    41  in establishing the API, since the `Finsupp` implementation of `R[X]` is well-shielded.
    42  
    43  Unlike the case of polynomials, I felt that the exponent notation was not too easy to use, as only
    44  natural exponents would be allowed.  Moreover, in the end, it seems likely that we should aim to

    46  convenient.
